description.describe_ch: 做 為管理工具的報表 ,如何在製作過程中嚴謹的監督與稽核 .事後如何依據報表以及其附註 ,一 窺公司管理良好與否以及產業特性和前景之預測。並收及上市櫃公司財務報表作各案研究與報告。使分析內容與財經媒體所敘述之公司情形作完整比對，以便純熟的應用各項比例指標。
description.describe_eh: As a tool for management, the financial statement must be understood from the process of procedures and fallowing the necessary control. The following events from the statements, we can understand whether the good or bad management, and the prediction of industry.

textBooks.tpb_book:
Financial Statement Analysis, 11/e
K. R. Subramanyam, University of Southern California
Financial Statement Analysis,  emphasizes effective business analysis and decision making by analysts, investors, managers, and other stakeholders of the company. It continues to set the standard in showing students the keys to effective financial statement analysis. The textbook is set up in a three part framework which makes this textbook one of the best-selling books in the market. It begins with an overview (chapters 1-2), followed by accounting analysis (chapters 3-6) and then financial analysis (chapters 7-11 and a Comprehensive Case). The book presents a balanced view of analysis, including both equity and credit analysis, and both cash-based and earnings-based valuation models. The eleventh edition is aimed at accounting and finance classes, and the professional audience–as it shows the relevance of financial statement analysis to all business decision makers.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol:
•Take all examinations (Mid-term exam and final exam).
•Participate in the weekly discussions.
•Turn in all work on time.
•Read the textbook pages listed in the syllabus and found on the weekly assignment pages.

gradeRuleDescribe.course_pol_en:
Attendance
Please be on time. The professor may ask you to leave if you're late without a good reason.
Don't leave early. It's not acceptable to complete attendance and then leave before class is over.
Return from breaks on time and be ready to continue.
Notify the professor in advance if you cannot attend class for a valid reason, such as illness or an emergency.
During Class
Pay attention. Avoid distractions like playing computer games, listening to music, wearing headphones, or watching movies.
Be respectful. Don't chat with other students while the professor is speaking. It disrupts the class and is disrespectful to the professor and your peers.
Participate actively. You are encouraged to engage in the class discussions.
Let one person speak at a time, including when answering questions.
During Presentations
Be respectful to your classmates. Avoid talking or making noise during presentations.
Listen to the presenter. All group members should avoid talking to each other while one person is presenting.
Stay in the room. Don't walk in or out of the classroom during a presentation unless it's an emergency. Wait until the presentation is finished.
Give constructive feedback and ask questions respectfully when it is appropriate.
gradeRuleDescribe.course_rem: Students who miss class will miss the discussion of the learning objective(s) covered during the class.  All students are expected to take good notes during each class, so those who miss class should first check with a trusted classmate to "catch up" on what was missed.
